t: This is 44 Tite Street, a building in Kensington and Chelsea, designed by Edward William Godwin. Godwin was a progressive architect and designer. He began in the strongly coloured Ruskinian Gothic style, inspired by The Stones of Venice, then moved to the Anglo-Japanese taste of the Aesthetic movement in the 1870s, after encountering Japanese culture at the 1862 International Exhibition in London. His influence can be seen in the later Arts and Crafts movement. So this house comes from one of the more forward-looking designers of Victorian Britain.
